## Design

### 2026-11-08: November 2: Planning the Circuit Design

**9h**

November 2: Planning the Circuit Design

So here we are in Week 5 the week of the project!

First of all I started by designing the circuit to figure out how everything would be connected and what the overall design would look like.

Initially I was thinking of using a Raspberry Pi Zero so I made one schematic for it. Then tried another version.. Later I realized that integrating everything into a single PCB would be more complex with the Raspberry Pi Zero.

![Screenshot 2026-11-08 103235](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/r1nSTxCFQ2zE35VmMrOpNVe2xLvWebY1/05fc2e572003e404af295fec06aeadcbcb6022f952a4136b13dc629c95e624cb.jpg)
So I decided to switch to an ESP32. I also added one component, the SSD module and modified the schematic accordingly.

![Screenshot 2026-11-08 103255](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/r1nSTxCFQ2zE35VmMrOpNVe2xLvWebY1/447c24e9876ea1e3177834892b05a739c16ed020683b97a61857b3921879a735.jpg)
Finally after two hours of experimenting with different designs I completed the final schematic!

Time spent: 2 hours.

November 3: PCB Schematic and Initial Design

Today I started working on the PCB schematic deciding which components would be required and how everything would be connected. This took me around one hour.

![Screenshot 2026-11-05 171723](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/r1nSTxCFQ2zE35VmMrOpNVe2xLvWebY1/b110738d2e94ddf2fe7719d1ec2c1f9e427d2f0e63b2c8538c98ab28b2301336.jpg)

After that I started working on the PCB design. First I made a sketch of the PCB layout, which took around two hours.

![Screenshot 2026-11-05 194529](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/r1nSTxCFQ2zE35VmMrOpNVe2xLvWebY1/840bb4aaa616f17947991a796e16b5b0a4438a2f67ae6a18068657e8d92ae9a3.jpg)

Then I started connecting all the components and routing the wires. Once the wiring was completed I checked the design using the Design Rules Checker (DRC).

![Screenshot 2026-11-05 175645](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/r1nSTxCFQ2zE35VmMrOpNVe2xLvWebY1/c77d825479cbb38ec58e8be8ef2b37a9cbe30b72d20a3ee3fb1451a5f4e3e64f.jpg)

November 5: Finalizing the Viewfinder Design

Today I focused on the viewfinder placement on the PCB.

At first I was thinking of making a slot for the viewfinder. I tried two sketches and tested the placement.

In the design I tried a different arrangement but later I realized that the viewfinder would not fit properly.

![WhatsApp Image 2026-11-08 at 11.10.34 AM](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/r1nSTxCFQ2zE35VmMrOpNVe2xLvWebY1/49fd031eeef390655377abc57e1701b318c28538736d06992decb9b17a7c85a1.jpg)
So I changed the design. Added grooves inside the PCB to hold the viewfinder correctly.

This took me about two hours of designing and making adjustments.

![pcb_3d_front](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/r1nSTxCFQ2zE35VmMrOpNVe2xLvWebY1/1f33d26e8e9c81c1fdca7274bd8dafca43c0f2c256561967417a7c1f08d40bf2.png)
Finally, after all the changes the design was complete!

Time spent: two hours.

### 2026-11-08: 6th November

**4h**

6th November

Today I began working on the circuit and code for the camera. I wrote all the code and built the entire circuit in Goofway making sure to add every component and connection required for the simulation. After four hours of focused work I finally tested the circuit. It worked perfectly just as I had hoped. The output matched what I wanted so all the time I spent on designing, coding and debugging was worth it. It was an joyful finish, to the project. I successfully completed my camera.
